claims.hypothesis: Can sites of current star formation be spatially separated from dense gas at ~90 pc?
claims.experiment: Compare 33/94.5 GHz continuum peaks with HCN/HCO+ moment 0 peaks
claims.result: Enuc. 2 peaks offset by ≈3 arcsec (~130 pc)
claims.finding: Resolution suffices to distinguish current star formation from fuel for future star formation

evidence.quote: this offset suggests that we have reached the spatial resolution at which we can reliably separate the fuel stockpiles from the current generation of star formation

claims.hypothesis: Is 33 GHz emission dominated by thermal free-free at the HII region peaks?
claims.experiment: 33-94.5 GHz spectral index and thermal decomposition
claims.result: mean thermal fractions 70-85%, near unity at peaks
claims.finding: Thermal fraction near unity at peaks

evidence.quote: The mean thermal fraction at 33 GHz among the three regions studied is 79% with a dispersion of 19%.

claims.hypothesis: Does dense gas fraction or dynamical state control SFE?
claims.experiment: Plot dense gas fraction and HCO+ velocity dispersion vs SFE for three regions
claims.finding: Dynamical state of dense gas matters more than abundance

evidence.quote: the dynamical state of the dense gas appears to have a larger impact on the star formation process than the actual fraction of dense gas

limitations_admitted.value: Only three regions; nuclear HCN cut off by bandpass; single-component fit poor for Enuc. 2

evidence.quote: the detection of HCN towards the nucleus is cut off by the bandpass at a radial velocity of $v_\mathrm{LSRK} \approx 800\mathrm{\,km\,s^{-1}}$
